title: Nvidia pledges $250 million to boost UK AI safety research
source_used: Nvidia's own press release on nvidianews.nvidia.com (full text). Reuters (pool source) returned HTTP 401.
key_facts: Nvidia announced a five-year compute donation valued at $250 million to strengthen the UK's agentic safety and security research capability (agentic = AI that acts on its own).
That is $50 million of compute access a year; the majority is for the wider UK AI safety and security research community.
A proportion goes to BOLD (led by the University of Oxford), SOFAIR (led by UCL) and Imperial College London.
Compute will be delivered through UK-based NVIDIA Cloud Partners with infrastructure hosted in the UK; "provider selection, technical architecture and commercial terms are to be agreed".
Research is to focus on secure agents, open-model security and real-world threat mitigations, including secure sandboxes and safety benchmarks.
Jensen Huang, founder and chief executive of Nvidia, said the donation will put accelerated computing in UK researchers' hands to "develop, test and strengthen safeguards".
Kanishka Narayan, the UK AI minister, called it "a vote of confidence" in UK frontier AI safety strength; Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds also commented.
quote_evidence: NVIDIA today announced a five-year compute donation valued at $250 million to strengthen the United Kingdom's agentic safety and security research capability.
The commitment will provide $50 million in compute access annually to support agentic safety and security research across the U.K.
Provider selection, technical architecture and commercial terms are to be agreed.
why_it_matters_hint: Nvidia is giving UK researchers computing power worth $250 million over five years to study how to make AI agents safe and secure.
notes: Source is Nvidia's own announcement, which also carries UK government quotes. The value is compute access, not cash. Reuters carried the story (headline seen, text unreadable, HTTP 401).
